newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel surprises as first-half net rises 13.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: SingTel surprises as first-half net rises 13.6 pct.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) beat market expectations on Friday with a 13.6 percent rise in first half net profits to Singapore $843.5 million (US$602.5 million), from S$742.5 million a year ago. SingTel, Southeast Asia's biggest telecoms group with a capitalisation of more than S$40 billion, said in a statement its turnover grew a healthy 10.5 percent in the six months to September 30, 1996, to S$2.17 billion from S$1.96 billion.
A Reuters survey of industry analysts had suggested the company's interim net profit would show a much more modest eight to nine percent rise to only around S$805 million.
"These results look better than we were expecting," said Gautam Kapoor, regional telecoms analyst at ING Barings.
SingTel said the half year continued to witness strong growth in the mobile communications and leased circuit businesses.
It said growth in the volume of international calls had been satisfactory but was not as robust as the growth in the same period last year due to slower growth in the Singapore economy.

"Despite the anticipated slower economic growth in the next few quarters, Singapore Telecom is confident of maintaining its double-digit earnings growth for the full year," Singapore Telecom chairman Koh Boon Hwee told a news conference.
Koh said SingTel's international direct dialing (IDD) traffic grew by 12.9 percent during the period.

He said a series of recent cuts in charges for IDD calls, which account for about 40 percent of SingTel's turnover, was designed to promote demand for international telephone calls but would also eventually eat into the company's margins.
"The impact of the IDD cuts will be felt in the second half," he said.
He said next year, 1997/98, would also see some pressure on margins as the company faced competition for the first time in its domestic paging market.
"A lot depends on how quickly the Singapore economy will grow," he said, but added, "It is our goal to still try to maintain double-digit profit growth in 1997."

Profits from SingTel's associated firms and joint ventures improved significantly during the first-half as its new investments in Belgian state telephone operator, Belgacom, and in PT Bukaka SingTel International in Indonesia began to pay off.
Overall, associates produced a profit of S$1.1 million, compared with a loss of S$31.1 million in the first half of the previous year.
SingTel said it had reduced its interest in several joint venture companies, including cable companies in Britain, during the period in line with its policy of rationalising its investments.
